newsitem.title: USA: DC CFO fires 165 city employees - spokesperson.
newsitem.headline: DC CFO fires 165 city employees - spokesperson.

text.p: The District of Columbia's chief financial officer, Anthony Williams, fired 165 city employees on Friday, in the largest such action to date by the financially strapped city, a spokesperson said.

"We are taking an adverse action today," Peggy Armstrong, director of communications for Williams, said in a telephone interview. "This is not a reduction in force. It is the result of a review of the employees' performance," she said.

Armstrong said the fired employees, who all worked on D.C. finances, "were notified by their supervisors today that their services are no longer needed." They will receive four weeks severance pay, she said.
Williams fired 68 people in the city's Office of Tax and Revenue and 36 in D.C.'s Department of Human Services, in the largest of the firings, Armstrong said.

He also fired 15 people at the University of the District of Columbia, 10 each at the Office of Finance and Treasury and the Metroplitan Police Department and eight each in the city controller's office and the D.C. Public Schools.

Williams also fired three each in his mission support center and in the Office of Pay and Retirement, and two each at D.C.'s public libraries and the office that oversees the city's multimillion dollar lottery, Armstrong said.
Armstrong said the firings should not come as a surprise. Williams has been saying for months that the city needs "the best possible work force because of its financial crisis.
